title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
why_read: A technically rich paper on counterfactual world models for robot action planning, offering a principled way to compare hypothetical outcomes rather than just predicting single futures.
analysis: WhatIf proposes a world model that can simulate what would happen under different candidate robot actions while keeping the underlying physical situation fixed, enabling fair comparison between choices. It builds a causal graph per action to track which objects are affected and uses a paired-comparison statistical technique to reduce estimation noise when ranking plans. This addresses a real limitation of typical world models, which predict outcomes of actions independently rather than comparing them under shared conditions. The approach is mathematically grounded, including a formal link between counterfactual variance and planning risk, making it a substantive contribution to robotic decision-making research.
